Question: A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

Options:
opa. Decreased sense of smell
opb. Numbness of the left cheek
opc. Preserved left lateral gaze
opd. Absent left corneal reflex
ope. Complete loss of vision of the left eye

These structures include cranial nerves III (oculomotor), IV (trochlear), V1 (ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve), and VI (abducens), as well as the superior ophthalmic vein. The most relevant symptom in this context would be related to the ophthalmic branch of the trigeminal nerve, which could cause numbness in the areas it innervates, such as the forehead and upper eyelid. However, the numbness of the left cheek is more associated with the maxillary branch (V2) of the trigeminal nerve, which is not directly affected by the superior orbital fissure. The preserved left lateral gaze suggests that the abducens nerve (VI) is functioning, which is not consistent with compression at the superior orbital fissure.
